evaluations.requirement_text: The system must provide a mobile application for both Android and iOS devices.
evaluations.feedback: Accurately reflects the source and is testable at a high level. The acceptance criterion is clear enough for platform availability verification. Minor improvement: define the minimum supported OS versions and clarify what 'core features' includes, otherwise platform parity may be disputed during testing.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must allow users to view current football news for their favorite teams.
evaluations.feedback: Good extraction from the source and mostly testable. However, 'current football news' is vague: define freshness expectations, source update frequency, and what happens when no favorite teams are configured. Acceptance should also specify whether news is filtered exclusively by favorites or merely prioritized.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must allow users to individually select preferred sports channels for news display.
evaluations.feedback: Correctly derived and reasonably testable. The main gap is ambiguity around behavior: does channel selection filter out unselected channels completely, rank selected channels higher, or both? Acceptance should explicitly state expected output rules and persistence of user selections across sessions.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must provide a live ticker for users to follow the results of their favorite teams live.
evaluations.feedback: Aligned with the source and understandable. Still, 'live' is underspecified and overlaps with FR-009 and FR-010. To improve, define whether the ticker shows only scores or also incidents (goals, cards, substitutions), and specify update expectations and behavior when no live match exists.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must provide coverage of leagues and competitions at national and international levels.
evaluations.feedback: Traceable to the source, but too broad to be strongly testable. 'Coverage' is undefined and could mean listings, results, standings, fixtures, news, or full match detail. 'All leagues and competitions' from the source was softened into a vague phrase. This requirement should be decomposed and specify what data elements are available per league/competition and any inclusion boundaries.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must provide detailed team information and player information.
evaluations.feedback: The intent is correct, but 'detailed information' is not measurable. Testers cannot determine pass/fail without defined fields such as squad, statistics, standings, biography, position, age, recent form, etc. Acceptance should enumerate minimum required information sets for team pages and player pages.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must integrate live stream links from supported broadcast providers and display them in the app when the live broadcast has begun.
evaluations.feedback: Good capture of the feature and generally testable. The phrase 'supported broadcast providers' needs explicit definition, otherwise scope is unstable. Acceptance should also address behavior before broadcast start, when a link is unavailable, and whether the app opens an in-app web view, deep link, or external provider app.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must display live stream links only when the applicable transmission rights are fulfilled for the user's country.
evaluations.feedback: Strong compliance-oriented requirement and faithful to the source. The key weakness is operational ambiguity: how is the user's country determined—device locale, account profile, IP geolocation, SIM, or a rights service? Acceptance should define the entitlement/rules check and expected failure behavior when rights are not valid or location cannot be determined.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must provide real-time retrieval and display of live results for users' favorite teams through an integrated live ticker module.
evaluations.feedback: This reflects the source, but it duplicates FR-004 and partially FR-010. 'Real-time' is not testable without latency thresholds. Improve by merging overlapping requirements or distinguishing them clearly: e.g., FR-004 for feature availability, FR-009 for update latency and result events, FR-010 for UI refresh behavior.

evaluations.requirement_text: The live ticker module must communicate with the user interface to display and continuously update current match data.
evaluations.feedback: This is more design/internal architecture than externally observable functionality. 'Communicate with the user interface' is implementation-oriented and weakly verifiable from a user perspective. Also, 'continuously update' is vague. Rewrite as an observable requirement such as 'the live ticker screen shall automatically refresh displayed match data within X seconds of receiving new live data without requiring manual refresh.'

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must retrieve live data for the live ticker from an external server via an API.
evaluations.feedback: Directly traceable, but it is largely architectural rather than user-facing. If architectural requirements are allowed, it is acceptable; otherwise it should be moved to a system design specification. The acceptance criterion is difficult to verify without inspecting implementation or logs. Add measurable expectations such as API availability fallback behavior, retry policy, and data validation handling.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must provide additional modules that allow users to individually configure the app through the user interface.
evaluations.feedback: This is too vague and inherits unclear wording from the source ('connect their own interface to the user interface'). 'Additional modules' and 'individually configure the app' are not defined, so it is not meaningfully testable. The requirement should be decomposed into explicit configurable capabilities, such as notification preferences, favorite teams, preferred channels, language, dark mode, or homepage layout, each with clear expected behavior.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must provide a notification function that, when activated by the user, delivers information about current events.
evaluations.feedback: The requirement is relevant but too broad. 'Current events' is undefined and overlaps with FR-016. To make this production-ready, specify event categories covered by generic notifications versus favorite-team notifications, delivery channels (push/in-app), opt-in/out behavior, and whether quiet hours or duplicate suppression apply.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must allow users to register and log in directly at app startup.
evaluations.feedback: Well aligned with the source and testable. The acceptance criterion clearly captures the startup flow. A useful enhancement would be to define supported authentication methods, required fields, and behavior for users who skip login if guest access is allowed.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must allow users to follow favorite clubs to personalize their experience.
evaluations.feedback: Clear, traceable, and testable. Good user-centered phrasing and acceptable acceptance criterion. Minor improvement: specify whether there is a limit on the number of favorite clubs and whether selections sync across devices for the same account.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must allow users to receive notifications about news or results of their favorite teams.
evaluations.feedback: Strong and well-scoped requirement derived directly from the source. The dependency on following a team and enabling notifications is properly captured. For stronger testability, add expected delivery timing and whether both pre-match/live/post-match result updates are included.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must allow users to share news and game reports directly from the app via social media.
evaluations.feedback: Good extraction and reasonably testable. Slight ambiguity remains around supported social media destinations and what content format is shared (link, title, summary, image). Acceptance should also state expected behavior if no compatible social apps are installed.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must remain usable offline when the app temporarily loses network connection.
evaluations.feedback: This comes from the source, but it is closer to a non-functional/operational resilience requirement than a pure functional one. More importantly, 'usable offline' is too vague. The requirement must specify exactly which features remain available offline—cached news, saved favorites, previously loaded team/player pages, settings changes, etc.—and how stale data is indicated.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must support evaluation of user feedback and app reviews to improve functionality.
evaluations.feedback: Poorly framed as a system requirement. The source describes an organizational/process activity, not necessarily an app feature. 'Support evaluation' is extremely vague, and the acceptance criterion weakly allows either 'system or supporting process,' which makes ownership and testability unclear. Unless the product includes a specific feedback analytics module, this should be reclassified as a business/process requirement or replaced with explicit in-app feedback collection/reporting functionality.

evaluations.requirement_text: The application must be fully loaded and ready to use within a maximum of 2 seconds after startup on supported Android and iOS devices.
evaluations.feedback: Excellent extraction: measurable, testable, and clearly tied to the source. Strong acceptance criterion. To make it fully production-grade, specify the test conditions: device classes, OS versions, cold vs warm start, network assumptions, and what 'ready to use' precisely means (first interactive screen visible, login prompt available, cached content loaded, etc.).

evaluations.requirement_text: The application must provide direct and easy access to information through the user interface.
evaluations.feedback: This is highly subjective and not testable in its current form. Terms like 'direct' and 'easy' are usability aspirations, not measurable criteria. The acceptance criterion still uses subjective language ('unnecessary navigation steps'). Replace with quantifiable usability constraints, e.g., 'Users shall reach live ticker, news, and favorites within no more than 2 taps from the home screen' or validated UX success metrics from usability testing.

evaluations.requirement_text: All modules and the user interface must remain consistent even when external server updates occur.
evaluations.feedback: Relevant but vague. 'Consistent' could mean layout stability, feature set stability, schema compatibility, or visual design continuity. Acceptance should define what must not change due to server updates, for example: navigation structure, module availability, and UI rendering shall not break when external data changes. Also clarify whether this refers to content updates or backend/API version changes.

evaluations.requirement_text: Registration and login shall be uncomplicated for users.
evaluations.feedback: This requirement is not testable. 'Uncomplicated' is purely subjective and the acceptance criterion repeats that subjectivity ('simple enough'). Convert this into measurable usability requirements, such as maximum number of steps, completion time, success rate in usability testing, password rules, error recovery, and percentage of users able to complete authentication without assistance.

evaluations.requirement_text: The application must function reliably even with limited network coverage.
evaluations.feedback: Important requirement, but 'reliably' and 'limited network coverage' are undefined. The acceptance criterion also lacks measurable thresholds. Improve by defining degraded network profiles (e.g., 3G, high latency, packet loss), allowed failure rates, timeout/retry behavior, and which features must still operate under such conditions.

evaluations.requirement_text: The application must support up to 100,000 simultaneous users on high-traffic match days without performance loss.
evaluations.feedback: Good and important scalability requirement directly derived from the source. The weakness is that 'without performance loss' is unrealistic and unmeasurable unless tied to specific service-level indicators. Add explicit thresholds for API response time, app screen load time, error rate, notification delay, and live ticker latency under 100,000 concurrent users.

evaluations.requirement_text: The application must undergo thorough testing and support processes before release to detect and resolve malfunctions early.
evaluations.feedback: This is largely a process requirement, not a product quality attribute in a testable NFR form. 'Thorough' is undefined, and 'support processes' is too broad. Rewrite as release quality gates, e.g., required automated test coverage, zero critical defects open, successful load/security tests, and incident support readiness criteria before release approval.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must process all personal data in compliance with the GDPR.
evaluations.feedback: Correctly derived and highly relevant. However, compliance statements are broad and difficult to verify unless decomposed. Strengthen with concrete obligations: lawful basis capture, consent where required, right-to-access/export/delete workflows, data minimization, retention limits, breach handling, and records of processing. As written it is directionally strong but too high-level for direct verification.
